$sources: Measures and colours: the as-built museum's lily colonies (windows/Source/MuseeVision/Nature/MuseeWaterLilies.cpp, BuildWaterLilies and AddNymphaea), which the owner approved; the colony rule round(2 + 8 x reach) pads is theirs.
The cultivar: Joseph Bory Latour-Marliac's hardy hybrid 'Marliacea Carnea' (Temple-sur-Lot, 1887), pale flesh-pink. Monet ordered his first water lilies from Latour-Marliac in 1894.

Ranges for hardy Nymphaea: pads 15-30 cm across, flowers 10-15 cm, on or just above the water (P. D. Slocum, Waterlilies and Lotuses, Timber Press 2005, the hardy hybrids). The as-built pads (radius 0.10-0.22 m) lie at the large end, as an established colony's do. To confirm against Slocum's entry for the cultivar.
name: Nymphaea × marliacea 'Carnea'
common: Latour-Marliac's pale pink hardy water lily
note: Pink: the petals flush from a near-white base to pink tips. Four plants in ten in flower in the museum's warm oval, as the as-built plan flowered four of ten.
